newsitem.title: HONG KONG: California governor makes Hong Kong freedom call.
newsitem.headline: California governor makes Hong Kong freedom call.

text.p: California governor Pete Wilson kicked off an eight-city Asian tour on Monday with a reminder that Hong Kong needs freedom to prosper beyond its reversion to Chinese sovereignty on July 1.

"Clearly the prescription is for continued freedom," Wilson said. "A communist regime is by definition not a free trade regime...(but this) is an opportunity for Beijing to demonstrate it is a ruler of wisdom."
Hong Kong is California's 10th largest trading partner, with exports to the territory rising 18 percent to nearly US$4 billion in 1995.
Hong Kong also ranks as California's seventh-largest foreign direct investor, with accumulated investment surpassing US$12 billion.
The post-transition relationship between the state and the territory will top the agenda at a private dinner on Monday with Hong Kong's future Chief Executive Tung Chee-hwa, Wilson said.
"We are interested in whether Hong Kong will continue in the future to be what it has been in the past -- a bastion of free trade," Wilson told reporters.
He also called for tougher enforcement of intellectual property piracy, an issue that brought the United States and China to the brink of a multibillion-dollar trade war in June.
Wilson, who said he supports China's inclusion in the World Trade Organisation, said more needs to be done to crack down on intellectual property theft from California's huge high-technology sector.
"We are very concerned about enforcement. I am told that a short subway ride from here software worth a couple of thousand (U.S. dollars) is being sold for virtually nothing," he said.
He will raise the issue with China's foreign trade and economic cooperation minister, Wu Yi, later in the tour.
California launched the 21-day trade mission following its emergence from a major recession that slashed state revenues by one-third and cost 750,000 jobs.

A number of business incentives, including corporate tax cuts and deregulation of the electricity sector, have helped to recover all jobs lost and allowed California to become the first U.S. state with a trillion-dollar economy.

"I've come to Asia to spread the word that California is not just back in business, but that we're exemplifying the same economic savvy and hustle that has made Hong Kong the envy of much larger nations around the world," Wilson said. -- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843 6441
